name: Frey Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Frey Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of unilateral sweating and flushing in the preauricular and temporal region triggered by gustatory stimuli
History of parotid gland surgery, trauma, or infection preceding symptom onset
Positive Minor starch-iodine test demonstrating gustatory sweating

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of gustatory sweating and flushing in the auriculotemporal region with a history of parotid trauma or surgery
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; Minor starch-iodine test can confirm gustatory sweating.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral gustatory sweating in preauricular and temporal region
pathognomonic.notes: Triggered by eating or thinking about food
searchTerms: one-sided sweating near ear and temple when eating
gustatory sweating on one side of face
sweating triggered by food on affected side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral facial flushing in auriculotemporal distribution during mastication
searchTerms: one-sided facial flushing near ear during chewing
unilateral redness in auriculotemporal area when eating
facial flushing triggered by mastication on one side

common.symptomName: Mild facial warmth or erythema in affected region during meals
searchTerms: mild warmth or redness on face during meals
facial erythema in affected area while eating
localized facial flushing with food intake

common.symptomName: Tingling or paresthesia in preauricular area
searchTerms: numbness or pins and needles in preauricular region

occasional.symptomName: Mild pain or discomfort in parotid region
occasional.notes: Usually transient and related to mastication
May occur due to altered salivary gland function

occasional.symptomName: Facial muscle twitching near affected area
Mild headache localized to temporal region
searchTerms: mild headache on side of head
sweating on both sides of face when eating

rare.symptomName: Synkinesis of facial muscles during mastication
rare.notes: Involuntary muscle movements linked to nerve regeneration
searchTerms: face muscles moving together during eating
involuntary face muscle contractions while chewing

rare.symptomName: Severe social embarrassment leading to psychiatric symptoms
rare.notes: Depression or anxiety secondary to symptoms

imaging: MRI or CT may show post-surgical changes in parotid region
No specific imaging abnormalities diagnostic for Frey syndrome
other: Positive Minor starch-iodine test indicating gustatory sweating
Clinical history of parotid trauma or surgery

distinguishingFeatures: Bilateral sweating without history of parotid trauma

redFlags: Sudden onset of unilateral facial swelling
Signs of infection or abscess in parotid region
Progressive neurological deficits involving facial nerve
references: Haider A, et al. Frey Syndrome: Clinical Features and Management. J Clin Neurosci. 2019.
Minor starch-iodine test in diagnosis of gustatory sweating. Dermatol Ther. 2017.
